entry.title: Fix description of indexes in client-side storage tutorial
entry.content:
Description

Reword the "Database initial setup" part of the client-side storage tutorial so it no longer calls the indexes a "schema" or "fields".

Motivation

The tutorial said that upgradeneeded is where we define the schema of the database, "that is, the set of columns (or fields) it contains", and described the two indexes as fields. IndexedDB doesn't have a schema like that. Indexes are only for looking records up by a property, and stored objects can have any properties whether or not they are indexed. A beginner could easily come away thinking they have to create an index for every property they want to store.

I kept the explanation short, following the direction in the issue, and didn't go into a longer comparison of indexes and schemas.

Additional details

  • https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/IDBObjectStore/createIndex

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #41274

entry.title: docs(css_custom_highlight_api): mention StaticRange for highlights that outlive DOM changes
entry.content:
Closes #46513

Summary of changes

In files/en-us/web/api/css_custom_highlight_api/index.md:

  • Updated the "Create ranges" section to note that text ranges can be defined using either Range or StaticRange objects.
  • Added a note explaining the performance trade-offs:
    • Live Range instances automatically track boundary mutations, but maintaining large numbers of live ranges across subsequent DOM updates can incur notable performance overhead.
    • StaticRange instances are lightweight and do not observe DOM mutations, making them ideal when highlights are static or when managing large collections of ranges (e.g. search query results), provided the application manually refreshes or recreates ranges if the underlying DOM changes.

entry.title: docs(webgl): clarify srcData allows null to allocate storage and fix uncompressed texture descriptions
entry.content:
Closes #46493

Summary of changes

  1. Clarify srcData: null allocation:
    • In WebGLRenderingContext.texImage2D() and WebGL2RenderingContext.texImage3D(), explicit mention is added that srcData may be null to allocate texture storage without uploading pixels. WebGL implementations initialize this allocated storage to zeros to prevent information leakage.
  2. Correct uncompressed texture parameter descriptions:
    • In texImage2D, texSubImage2D, texImage3D, and texSubImage3D, srcData was described as "containing the compressed texture data". That wording was a copy-paste remnant from compressedTexImage2D / compressedTexImage3D. These methods handle uncompressed image/pixel data, so the description now accurately specifies "containing the image pixel data".

Verification

  • Ran npx prettier -c on all 4 modified files (Passed).
  • Ran npx markdownlint-cli2 on all 4 modified files (Passed — 0 issues).
  • Ran npx cspell on all 4 modified files (Passed — 0 issues).

entry.title: FF161 Clipboard API web custom formats: docs fixes
entry.content:
FF161 enables support for Clipboard API web custom formats (MIME types prefixed with web ) by default in https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2053725

Summary below, but mostly this is better cross-linking.

This fixes some gaps in the custom formats docs:

  • ClipboardItem(), ClipboardItem, ClipboardItem.types, ClipboardItem.getType() and ClipboardItem.supports() now mention and link to custom formats.
  • Clipboard.write(): NotAllowedError also covers unsupported types, including a web type that isn't a correctly structured MIME type.
  • Clipboard API overview: security note that custom format data may have been written by another site or application.
  • Minor: a typo, and reload(true) → reload() in the examples.

Related docs work can be tracked in #46463

entry.title: [Technical review] BiDi emulation module - `setGeolocationOverride` command
entry.content:
Description

This PR adds the page for emulation.setGeolocationOverride command, with corresponding updates to the module overview page and the sidebar.

Note

The Firefox note in BCD explicitly states that the global configuration is not yet supported.
My testing in Chrome shows the same limitation: omitting both scope selectors returns invalid argument: “Either user contexts or browsing contexts must be provided”. However, there's no such note for Chrome in BCD.

The current version of the page aligns with the spec to say that session-wide overrides are applied when neither contexts nor userContexts is specified. Let me know if this needs to be changed to the implemented behaviour instead.

Spec link
